name: Classic Idli
description: Soft and fluffy steamed rice-and-dal idlis served hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
steps: Check that your fermented batter is light, aerated, and doubled in volume. Stir gently once from bottom to top without knocking out the natural air bubbles.
Add 2 cups of water to the idli steamer or cooker and bring to a rolling boil on high heat before placing the plates inside.
Grease the idli moulds lightly with sesame oil or pure cow ghee. Ladle batter into each mould until 3/4th full so the idlis have space to expand.
Place the stand in the steamer, cover tightly with the lid (without pressure weight), and steam on medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let rest undisturbed for 2 minutes. Sprinkle a few drops of cool water on the back of the plates, then slide a wet spoon around the edges to unmould silky soft idlis.
Serve piping hot on a banana leaf alongside fresh coconut chutney, spicy tomato chutney, and aromatic tiffin sambar.

name: Chitti Idli (Button Idli)
description: Cute mini bite-sized idlis dipped in a bowl of hot sambar with a spoonful of melted ghee.
steps: Lightly grease mini-button idli moulds with melted pure cow ghee.
Carefully ladle 1 small teaspoon of fermented batter into each button cavity.
Steam in a preheated steamer on high flame for exactly 7 to 8 minutes until toothpicks inserted come out clean.
While hot, unmould the mini idlis using a small butter knife or teaspoon.
Place 15 to 20 hot button idlis directly into a wide shallow bowl, pour 2 generous ladles of boiling hot aromatic sambar all over them so they submerge completely.
Crown with a dollop of pure desi cow ghee, garnish with finely chopped fresh coriander, and let sit for 1 minute before eating so the idlis soak up the spiced lentil broth.

name: Ragi Idli
description: Healthy, earthy idlis made with finger millet flour (ragi), packed with fiber and calcium.
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine 1 cup ragi (finger millet) flour with 1 cup fermented urad dal batter, 0.5 cup fresh thick curd, and 1 tsp salt.
Whisk smoothly into a lump-free, pourable thick batter. Cover and rest for 15 minutes to allow the ragi flour to absorb the moisture.
Bring water to a boil in your steamer pot.
Grease idli plates with sesame oil, ladle the dark purple-brown ragi batter into the moulds.
Steam on medium-high heat for 12 to 14 minutes until firm and fully cooked through.
Rest for 2 minutes, unmould gently, and serve warm with a spicy roasted peanut chutney or allam (ginger) pachadi.

name: Thatte Idli
description: Famous Karnataka-style plate idli: large, super soft, and spongy, smeared with podi and butter.
steps: For authentic Bidadi-style thatte idli, ensure your batter contains soaked poha (flattened rice) blended along with the idli rice and urad dal for extreme sponginess.
Grease wide, flat thatte plates (or flat steel plates) generously with pure ghee or sesame oil.
Pour a large ladle (about 1 cup) of batter into the center and tilt the plate gently so it spreads into a wide, even disc.
Steam in a large steamer on high flame for 12 to 15 minutes until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let cool for 2 minutes. Run a wet flat knife along the outer edge and slide the giant plate idli onto a banana leaf.
Generously dust the entire top with spicy gun powder (chutney podi) and place a generous pat of fresh melting white butter right in the center.

name: Kanchipuram Idli
description: Traditional temple idli seasoned with coarsely crushed black pepper, cumin seeds, dry ginger, and cashews.
steps: Ensure your idli batter is ground coarsely (not silky smooth) to give the authentic temple texture.

For the royal tempering: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan. Crackle cumin seeds, coarsely crushed black peppercorns, finely minced fresh ginger, 10 halved cashews, and fresh curry leaves until aromatic and cashews turn golden.
Pour the sizzling ghee tadka along with 0.5 tsp dry ginger powder (sukku) and a pinch of hing directly into the coarse batter; fold gently.
Grease cylindrical steel tumblers, banana leaf cups, or traditional kanchipuram moulds with ghee.
Pour batter until 3/4th full and steam on medium-high flame for 18 to 20 minutes (since these idlis are denser and larger).
Unmould, slice into thick rounds if cooked in tumblers, and serve warm with spicy coconut chutney and idli podi.

name: Oats Idli
description: Quick, light instant idlis made with roasted oats, curd, mustard tempering, and grated carrots.
steps: Dry roast 1 cup rolled oats in a pan on medium-low flame for 4 minutes until warm and nutty. Cool and grind into a coarse flour.
In the same pan, heat 1 tsp oil; fry mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, finely chopped green chillies, grated ginger, and curry leaves.
In a bowl, combine the roasted oats flour, 0.5 cup semolina (rava), the prepared tempering, 1 finely grated carrot, and 1 cup fresh whisked curd.
Mix into a thick batter and let rest for 5 minutes. If batter thickens too much, add 2-3 tbsp water and a pinch of baking soda or eno.
Ladle into greased idli plates and steam immediately on high heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Serve warm with refreshing mint-coconut chutney for a light, fiber-rich breakfast.

name: Plain Dosa (Sada Dosa)
description: Crispy, paper-thin golden crepe made on a hot cast iron tawa with fermented batter.
steps: Heat a seasoned heavy cast-iron tawa on medium-high heat until hot. Splash a few drops of water; if they sizzle and dance off, wipe the surface with an onion half dipped in oil.
Pour a large ladle of well-fermented batter right into the center of the tawa.
Using the flat base of the ladle, spread the batter in smooth, quick outward concentric circles to form a thin, even crepe.
Immediately drizzle 1 teaspoon of oil or pure desi ghee all along the edges and across the surface.
Cook on medium-high flame without flipping until the edges curl up naturally and the underside turns a beautiful uniform golden brown.
Fold the dosa in half or roll into a cylinder and transfer to a plate immediately. Serve with fresh coconut chutney and piping hot sambar.

name: Masala Dosa
description: The classic restaurant favorite: crispy golden dosa stuffed with comforting spiced potato masala.
steps: Prepare the potato masala: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, chana dal, curry leaves, and green chillies. Sauté sliced onions until soft; add turmeric, salt, boiled coarsely mashed potatoes, and 3 tbsp water. Simmer for 3 minutes until moist and aromatic, finish with fresh coriander.
Heat your cast-iron tawa until very hot, splash water to check temperature, and wipe clean.
Ladle batter onto the center and spread thinly in concentric circles.
Drizzle pure cow ghee or butter generously around the borders and over the top. Roast on medium flame until golden brown and super crisp.
Spread a generous scoop of the warm potato masala across the center of the roasting dosa.
Fold both sides over the filling or roll into a cylinder, and serve piping hot with coconut chutney and tiffin sambar.

name: Onion Dosa
description: Crisp dosa topped with finely chopped onions, fresh green chillies, and coriander that caramelize on the pan.
steps: Finely dice 1 large onion, 2 green chillies, and fresh coriander leaves; mix together in a bowl with a pinch of cumin seeds.
Heat your tawa, grease lightly with oil, and pour a ladle of dosa batter, spreading it into a thin circular crepe.
Immediately, while the top batter is still wet, generously sprinkle a handful of the chopped onion-chilli mixture evenly across the entire surface.
Gently press the onions down with a flat spatula so they adhere into the batter.
Drizzle 1 tbsp oil around the circumference. Once the bottom is golden, flip the dosa for 30 to 45 seconds to let the onions caramelize into sweet golden perfection.
Flip back, fold, and serve hot with spicy tomato-garlic chutney.

name: Ghee Dosa (Ghee Roast)
description: Extra crispy, deep-golden crepe roasted lavishly in pure desi cow ghee.
steps: Prepare a well-fermented, slightly thin dosa batter for maximum crispiness.
Heat the cast-iron griddle on high heat, splash water droplets, and wipe clean with a cloth.
Spread a ladle of batter thinly from center outwards into a wafer-thin circle.
Ladle 2 tablespoons of pure desi cow ghee generously around the outer rim and across the top of the dosa.
Roast on medium flame; the ghee will fry the bottom to an intense, fragrant mahogany-gold crunch.
Roll into a tall showstopper cone (roast cone) or double fold, and serve smoking hot.

name: Rava Dosa
description: Lacy, wafer-crisp instant semolina dosa studded with whole cumin seeds, black pepper, and ginger.
steps: In a mixing bowl, whisk 0.5 cup rava (semolina), 0.5 cup rice flour, 2 tbsp maida, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp crushed black pepper, minced ginger, chopped green chillies, curry leaves, salt, and 2.5 cups water into a very thin, watery buttermilk-like batter. Rest for 15 minutes.
Stir the batter thoroughly from the bottom before each dosa, as rava tends to settle down.

Heat a cast-iron tawa until smoking hot. Do NOT spread with a ladle; instead, splash/pour a cup of thin batter from 3 inches height starting from the outer edge toward the center, allowing natural lace holes to form.
Drizzle 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee into all the holes and around the outer border.
Cook on medium-low flame for 3 to 4 minutes without disturbing until the edges turn reddish-brown and crisp up completely. Fold and serve with ginger chutney.

name: Pesarattu
description: Nutritious Andhra green gram crepe made from whole soaked moong dal, ginger, and green chillies.
steps: Soak 1 cup whole green gram (sabut moong) in water for at least 4 to 6 hours or overnight.
Drain and grind the soaked moong with 1 inch fresh ginger, 3 green chillies, 1 tsp cumin seeds, and 0.5 cup water into a smooth, pourable batter. Add salt to taste (no fermentation needed).
Heat a tawa on medium heat, pour a ladle of green batter, and spread into a medium-thin circle.
Immediately top with finely diced raw onions and a sprinkle of whole cumin seeds; press lightly with a spatula.
Drizzle oil or ghee around the edges and cook on medium heat until the bottom turns golden-brown and crisp.
Flip for 30 seconds to lightly toast the onions, flip back, fold in half, and serve hot with spicy sweet-tangy Andhra ginger chutney (Allam Pachadi).

name: Set Dosa
description: Set of three super soft, spongy, thick mini dosas that melt in your mouth, served with veg sagu.
steps: Make sure your batter contains flattened rice (poha) and thick curd, fermented overnight into an airy, frothy sponge batter.
Heat a tawa on medium-low heat and grease lightly with oil.
Pour a thick ladle of batter in the center. Do NOT spread thin; let it naturally spread into a small, thick 5-inch circle.
Cover the pan with a lid immediately. The steam trapped inside will create hundreds of tiny aerated holes on the surface.
Cook for 2 minutes on low flame until the top is fully set and spongy like a cloud. Do not flip.
Serve traditionally as a 'set' of three soft spongy dosas stacked together, accompanied by vegetable sagu and coconut chutney.

name: Mysore Masala Dosa
description: Famous Bangalore/Mysore style dosa coated with spicy red garlic-chilli chutney and stuffed with potato bhaji.
steps: Prepare the fiery red chutney: Sauté garlic cloves, soaked Byadgi red chillies, roasted chana dal, onion, and tamarind; blend into a thick, spicy, fragrant red paste.
Heat a cast-iron tawa until smoking hot, wipe with a damp cloth, and spread batter thinly into a large circle.
Drizzle melted butter or ghee along the perimeter.
As the dosa begins to turn golden, drop a generous tablespoon of the red garlic-chilli paste in the center and smear it evenly across the entire inner surface using a spatula.
Place a scoop of spiced potato bhaji in the middle.
Let the bottom roast to a deep mahogany, crackling crispness. Fold into a neat envelope or triangle and serve with coconut chutney.

name: Egg Dosa
description: Street-style crisp dosa with a fresh egg cracked and spiced directly on top while roasting.
steps: Heat your tawa, wipe clean, and spread a ladle of dosa batter into a wide thin circle.
Drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edges and let it cook for 30 seconds until the batter sets slightly.
Crack a fresh farm egg directly in the center of the roasting dosa.
Using a spoon or spatula, break the yolk and spread the egg evenly across the entire surface of the dosa.
Immediately season with a pinch of salt, freshly cracked black pepper, finely chopped onions, green chillies, and coriander.
Drizzle oil over the egg, flip the dosa carefully, and cook on medium flame for 1 minute until the egg is completely cooked, fragrant, and golden.
Flip back, fold in half, and serve hot with chicken gravy or spicy tomato chutney.

name: Poori
description: Puffed, golden whole-wheat deep-fried breads, crispy on the outside and hollow inside.
steps: In a wide bowl, mix 2 cups whole wheat flour with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp oil, and lukewarm water added in small increments.
Knead into a firm, stiff dough (a stiff dough prevents pooris from absorbing excess oil). Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 10 minutes.
Pinch small lemon-sized balls of dough. Roll each ball with light oil (avoid dry flour dusting as it burns in the oil) into a 4-inch round disc of even medium thickness.
Heat oil in a deep kadai on high flame until very hot (test with a tiny speck of dough; it should rise to the surface in 1 second).
Gently slide one rolled dough disc into the hot oil. Immediately tap the center lightly with the back of a slotted skimmer ladle; the steam will trap and balloon the poori up completely!
Flip the puffed poori, fry the other side for 5 seconds until light golden, remove with the skimmer, drain on paper towels, and serve immediately while puffed.

name: Chapati
description: Everyday soft, thin whole-wheat flatbread cooked on an iron tawa with a light brush of ghee.
steps: Combine 2 cups whole wheat flour with 0.5 tsp salt and gradually add warm water; knead for 5 minutes into a soft, supple, pliable dough. Smear with 1 tsp oil, cover, and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into smooth golf-ball sized rounds. Dust lightly with wheat flour and roll out evenly using a rolling pin into a thin 6 to 7-inch circle.
Heat an iron tawa on medium-high. Place the rolled chapati on the hot tawa.
Cook for 25-30 seconds until tiny air bubbles appear on the surface; flip over.
Cook the second side for 30 seconds, pressing gently with a clean folded kitchen towel or spatula around the edges; the chapati will puff up like a balloon.
Transfer to a plate, immediately brush with warm pure cow ghee, and stack inside an insulated roti box to stay soft for hours.

name: Puri Bhaji
description: The classic Indian breakfast pairing: puffed hot pooris served with mild yellow spiced potato curry.
steps: For the potato bhaji: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan, crackle mustard seeds, cumin, hing, green chillies, grated ginger, and curry leaves. Add sliced onions and cook until soft and translucent.

Add 0.5 tsp turmeric, salt, and 3 boiled potatoes coarsely crushed with your fingers. Pour 1 cup of warm water and simmer on medium flame for 5 minutes until the curry thickens to a comforting gravy. Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.
For pooris: Knead a stiff dough with wheat flour, salt, and water. Roll into small even discs.
Deep fry in smoking hot oil, pressing gently with a slotted ladle so they puff up into hollow golden balloons.
Drain quickly and serve 3 piping hot, crisp puffed pooris immediately alongside a generous bowl of hot potato bhaji and sliced red onions.

name: Upma
description: Simple, comforting South Indian semolina breakfast tempered with mustard, ginger, and curry leaves.
steps: Heat a dry pan on medium-low flame. Add 1 cup semolina (rava) and roast slowly for 4-5 minutes, stirring continuously until fragrant and warm (do not let it brown). Transfer to a plate.
In the same kadai, heat 2 tbsp oil or pure cow ghee. Add 1 tsp mustard seeds; when they crackle, add 1 tsp chana dal, 1 tsp urad dal, and fry until golden.
Add finely chopped ginger, 2 slit green chillies, sliced onions, and fresh curry leaves; sauté until onions turn translucent.
Pour 2.5 cups of water and 1 tsp salt into the kadai; bring to a rolling, bubbling boil on high flame.

Lower the heat to medium. Slowly pour the roasted rava into the boiling water in a steady stream with one hand while stirring continuously with a wooden spatula in the other hand to prevent any lumps from forming.
Cover tightly with a lid and cook on low heat for 3 minutes until all water is absorbed. Turn off flame, drizzle 1 tbsp pure ghee on top, rest covered for 2 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

name: Rava Upma
description: Rich, homestyle upma loaded with golden cashews, sweet sliced onions, and a spoon of melted ghee.
steps: In a kadai, heat 2 tbsp pure cow ghee. Add 10-12 halved cashews and fry on low heat until golden brown and crunchy; remove and set aside.
In the remaining hot ghee, roast 1 cup Bombay rava for 4 minutes until warm, nutty, and aromatic; transfer to a plate.
Add 1 more tablespoon of ghee/oil to the pan. Crackle mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, grated ginger, curry leaves, and sliced onions; sauté until onions soften.
Pour 2.5 cups water, add salt to taste, and bring to a vigorous rolling boil.
Stream the roasted rava in gradually while whisking continuously to keep it silky smooth and lump-free.
Cover with a tight lid, simmer on low heat for 3 minutes, then fold in the golden fried cashews and a teaspoon of fresh lemon juice before serving.

name: Pongal
description: Creamy, heartwarming rice and moong dal khichdi tempered with whole black pepper, cumin, and cashews in ghee.
steps: Dry roast 0.5 cup yellow moong dal in a pressure cooker on low flame for 3 minutes until nutty and fragrant (do not brown).
Add 1 cup raw rice (or leftover cooked rice), wash thoroughly, and add 4.5 cups of water with 1 tsp salt.
Pressure cook on medium flame for 4 to 5 whistles until the rice and dal are completely soft, creamy, and easily mashable.
Open the cooker and lightly mash the rice-dal mixture with the back of a ladle into a porridge-like consistency.

For the royal tempering: Heat 3 tablespoons of pure desi cow ghee in a small pan. Add 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 10 whole cashews, 1 inch finely chopped ginger, and fresh curry leaves; fry on low heat until cashews turn golden.
Pour the sizzling ghee tadka directly over the mashed pongal, stir thoroughly, and serve steaming hot with coconut chutney and medu vada.

name: Ven Pongal
description: Temple-style white savory pongal, silky smooth and rich with pure cow ghee and roasted spices.
steps: In a pressure cooker, combine 1 cup raw rice and 0.5 cup roasted yellow moong dal with 5 cups of water and 1 tsp salt.
Cook for 5 whistles on medium flame until ultra-soft and silky smooth.
Mash the mixture lightly with a wooden ladle while steaming hot.
In a separate tadka pan, heat 4 generous tablespoons of pure cow ghee on medium flame.
Crackle 1.5 tsp crushed black peppercorns, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 12 whole cashews, grated ginger, and curry leaves until the cashews are rich golden and the pepper releases its pungent aroma.
Pour the bubbling ghee tempering over the pongal, mix well, and serve piping hot on a banana leaf alongside authentic tiffin sambar.

name: Pesarattu Upma (MLA Pesarattu)
description: Andhra's ultimate breakfast combo: a crisp green moong dosa stuffed with hot savory rava upma inside.
steps: First, cook a quick batch of homestyle savory rava upma loaded with cashews and ghee; keep it warm.
Grind soaked whole green moong dal with fresh ginger, green chillies, and cumin into a smooth batter.
Heat a cast-iron tawa on medium-high heat, pour a ladle of green moong batter, and spread into a thin circle.
Sprinkle finely diced onions, green chillies, and cumin seeds on top; drizzle 1 tablespoon of pure cow ghee around the edges.
Roast until the bottom turns deep golden-brown and crispy.
Place a generous scoop of hot savory rava upma right in the center of the crisp green dosa.
Fold both sides over the upma into a roll, slide onto a plate, and serve immediately with Andhra ginger chutney (Allam Pachadi).

name: Uttapam
description: Thick, soft fermented pancake with a golden crisp base and spongy pillowy top.
steps: Ensure your fermented dosa batter is thick (ladle-coating consistency, not thin like dosa batter).
Heat a tawa on medium heat and smear with a few drops of oil.
Pour a generous, thick ladle of batter into the center. Do NOT spread it out thin; let it settle naturally into a thick 6-inch round pancake.
Drizzle oil or ghee around the edges.
Cover the tawa with a domed lid and cook on medium-low flame for 2.5 minutes until the base turns golden and the top is cooked and aerated with tiny holes.
Flip gently and cook the other side for 1 minute until lightly toasted. Serve warm with sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Onion Uttapam
description: Thick savory pancake loaded with sweet caramelized onions, green chillies, and fresh coriander.
steps: Finely chop 1 large onion, 2 green chillies, and fresh coriander leaves.
Heat a tawa on medium flame, drizzle a few drops of oil, and pour a thick ladle of fermented batter into a 6-inch pancake.
Immediately, while the top batter is still wet, press a generous handful of the chopped onions, chillies, and coriander firmly into the batter with your fingers.
Drizzle 1 tablespoon of pure ghee or oil around the outer rim and over the onions.
Cover with a lid and cook on medium-low for 2 minutes until the base is crisp and cooked through.
Flip the uttapam carefully and cook on medium flame for 1 to 2 minutes so the onions press against the hot griddle and caramelize into sweet, golden perfection.
Flip back and serve hot with spicy tomato chutney.

name: Appam
description: Kerala bowl-shaped fermented rice pancake with a soft spongy cloud center and crispy lace edges.
steps: Prepare the fermented batter using raw rice, cooked rice, coconut milk, and a pinch of yeast; ferment overnight until frothy and bubbly.
Heat an authentic curved non-stick or seasoned cast-iron appachatti (appam pan) on medium-low flame.
Lightly grease the center with oil using a paper towel.

Pour a ladle of batter into the center of the pan. Immediately hold both handles of the pan, lift it slightly, and swirl it once in a complete circular motion so a thin layer coats the curved sides while the excess batter pools in the center.
Cover with the lid and cook on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes without flipping.

Remove the lid: the edges should be papery, crisp, and lacy, while the center remains a thick, spongy, cloud-soft white pillow. Slide onto a plate and serve with sweetened coconut milk or vegetable stew.

name: Medu Vada
description: Crunchy golden doughnut-shaped lentil fritters with a crisp exterior and airy, fluffy inside.
steps: Soak 1 cup whole skinless urad dal in water for 3 to 4 hours; drain completely.

Grind the dal in a wet grinder or mixer using only 2 to 3 tablespoons of ice-cold water (cold water prevents the batter from heating up and keeps it airy). Beat the batter with your hands in one direction for 3 minutes until light, fluffy, and white (test: a drop of batter should float on a bowl of water).
Fold in 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, 1 inch finely chopped ginger, 2 minced green chillies, fresh curry leaves, and salt.
Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium heat.
Wet your palms with water. Take a lemon-sized portion of batter, shape into a smooth ball on your wet fingers, and press a hole in the center with your thumb to create the doughnut shape.

Gently slide the shaped vada into the hot oil. Fry on medium flame for 3 to 4 minutes, flipping occasionally, until uniformly deep golden-brown and crackling crisp on the outside while staying light and airy inside. Drain and serve immediately with hot sambar.

name: Punugulu
description: Popular Andhra street snack: crisp bite-sized golden balls made from leftover idli or dosa batter.
steps: Take 2 cups of leftover, well-fermented idli or dosa batter in a mixing bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons of rice flour or maida to absorb excess moisture and give a crisp outer shell.
Add 1 finely chopped onion, 2 minced green chillies, 1 tsp cumin seeds, fresh curry leaves, and a pinch of salt; whisk into a thick dropping consistency.
Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium flame until hot.
Wet your fingers in water, pinch small bite-sized cherry-sized portions of batter, and drop them gently into the hot oil.
Deep-fry on medium heat, stirring continuously with a slotted ladle so they fry evenly on all sides into crunchy, golden-brown balls.
Drain on paper towels and serve piping hot with spicy peanut chutney or Andhra palli pachadi.

name: Paratha (Plain Flaky)
description: Crispy, multi-layered golden whole-wheat flatbread cooked with pure ghee on a tawa.
steps: In a bowl, knead 2 cups whole wheat flour with 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tsp oil, and warm water into a soft, smooth dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into smooth balls. Roll a ball into a 5-inch circle, spread 0.5 tsp pure cow ghee evenly on top, and dust with a pinch of dry flour.
Fold the circle in half into a semi-circle, spread a drop of ghee, and fold again into a triangle (or pleat like a fan and roll into a pinwheel spiral for lachha layers).
Roll the folded dough gently into an even triangle or round flatbread without pressing too hard, to preserve the internal layers.
Place on a hot tawa. Cook for 30 seconds until tiny bubbles appear; flip over.

Brush both sides generously with pure cow ghee and press the edges gently with a spatula on medium heat until golden brown spots appear and the layers separate into flaky, crispy goodness. Serve warm with curd and pickle.

name: Aloo Paratha
description: Classic Punjabi comfort: stuffed flatbread loaded with spiced mashed potatoes, served with butter.
steps: For the stuffing: Boil, peel, and thoroughly mash 3 large potatoes. Add 2 finely minced green chillies, 1 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp dry mango powder (amchur), 0.5 tsp garam masala, chopped fresh coriander, and salt; mix into a smooth, flavorful potato mixture.
Knead a soft, pliable whole wheat dough (the dough must be as soft as the filling so it rolls out without bursting).
Take a ball of dough, flatten the edges into a small cup, and place an equal-sized ball of potato filling in the center.
Bring the dough edges together over the filling, pinch to seal tightly at the top, and flatten gently with your palms.
Dust with dry flour and roll out very gently with light, even pressure into a 7-inch round paratha.
Place on a hot tawa. Cook the first side for 30 seconds, flip, spread 1 tablespoon of butter or ghee, flip again, and baste the other side.
Griddle on medium-high heat, pressing the edges until puffed, crisp, and speckled with golden-brown spots. Serve steaming hot with a melting slab of white butter, thick curd, and spicy mango pickle.

name: Veg Fried Rice
description: Indo-Chinese street-style wok-tossed long grain rice with crisp colorful vegetables and spring onions.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large wok or kadai on the highest heat until smoking.
Add finely minced garlic and sliced white parts of spring onion; toss for 20 seconds.
Add finely chopped carrots, French beans, and cabbage; stir-fry vigorously for 2 minutes to keep them crunchy.
Add cold, separated day-old cooked rice, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp vinegar, crushed black pepper, and salt.
Toss continuously on high flame for 2 minutes, finish with green spring onion greens, and serve hot.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description: Fluffy rice scrambled with fresh farm eggs, cracked black pepper, garlic, and scallions.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a hot wok. Pour 2 whisked eggs seasoned with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Quickly scramble into soft, fluffy curds on medium flame for 1 minute; remove and set aside.
In the same wok, heat 1 tbsp oil on high flame, sauté minced garlic and spring onions until fragrant.
Add cold cooked rice, scrambled eggs, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and a generous pinch of crushed black pepper.
Toss vigorously on high flame for 2 minutes so the rice grains get coated in egg aroma. Garnish with scallions.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
description: Diced tender chicken breast tossed in a smoking wok with basmati rice, vegetables, and soy sauce.
steps: Marinate small diced boneless chicken with 0.5 tsp soy sauce, cornstarch, pepper, and salt for 10 minutes.
Sear chicken in a smoking hot wok with 2 tbsp oil until golden and fully cooked (about 3-4 minutes); push to one side.
Crack 1 egg into the wok and scramble quickly.
Toss in minced garlic, finely diced carrots, beans, and spring onion whites for 1 minute.
Add chilled cooked rice, 1 tbsp soy sauce, white pepper, and toss continuously on high flame until grains dance.

name: Schezwan Fried Rice
description: Fiery, spicy street-style fried rice infused with red chilli Schezwan sauce, garlic, and crunchy vegetables.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high flame. Add minced garlic, ginger, and sliced celery or spring onions.
Add diced carrots, capsicum, and cabbage; stir-fry for 1.5 minutes on high heat.
Add 2 generous tablespoons of fiery red Schezwan sauce and 1 tsp soy sauce; mix until bubbling and fragrant.
Tip in cold separated cooked rice, toss vigorously on high flame until every grain turns spicy bright red.
Garnish with chopped spring onion greens and serve with Manchurian gravy.

name: Paneer Fried Rice
description: Golden pan-seared paneer cubes tossed with fragrant basmati rice, bell peppers, and oriental spices.
steps: Cut fresh paneer into small 1 cm cubes. Shallow fry in 1 tbsp oil or ghee until light golden; drain.
In the same pan on high heat, sauté minced garlic and diced bell peppers (capsicum) for 1 minute.
Add cold cooked basmati rice, golden paneer cubes, soy sauce, and crushed black pepper.
Gently toss on medium-high flame without breaking the paneer cubes until heated through.
Finish with fresh spring onion greens.

name: Mushroom Fried Rice
description: Earthy button mushrooms stir-fried on high heat with garlic, spring onions, and seasoned rice.
steps: Slice button mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and pat dry completely.
Heat 2 tbsp oil or butter on high flame; add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms.
Sauté on high heat without crowding until mushrooms release moisture and turn caramelized golden brown.
Add spring onions, cold cooked rice, light soy sauce, and lots of cracked black pepper.
Toss on high heat for 2 minutes and serve steaming hot.

name: Garlic Fried Rice
description: Aromatic burnt garlic flavored fried rice with crispy golden garlic chips and scallions.
steps: Thinly slice 8 cloves of garlic into chips. Fry in 2 tbsp oil on low flame until crisp and golden brown; drain and set aside.
In the remaining garlic-infused oil, add 1 tbsp finely minced raw garlic and sauté on high heat for 30 seconds.
Add cold cooked rice, a dash of light soy sauce, salt, and white pepper.
Toss on high flame until every grain is infused with toasted garlic aroma.
Turn off heat, mix in chopped spring onions, and top with the crispy golden garlic chips.

name: Mixed Fried Rice
description: Deluxe combination fried rice loaded with chicken, eggs, prawns, and colorful vegetables.
steps: Sear bite-sized chicken pieces and cleaned deveined prawns in 2 tbsp oil until cooked; set aside.
Scramble 2 eggs in the hot wok and add back the cooked chicken and prawns.
Toss in minced garlic, shredded cabbage, carrots, and spring onions on smoking high heat.
Add cold cooked long-grain rice, 1 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce (or dark soy), and black pepper.
Toss continuously on high flame for 2-3 minutes for a true street-style smoky wok hei flavor.

name: Lemon Rice (Chitranna)
description: Zesty, turmeric-tinted tempered rice with crunchy roasted peanuts, mustard seeds, and fresh curry leaves.
steps: Spread warm cooked rice on a wide plate to cool; drizzle 1 tsp sesame oil and 0.5 tsp turmeric over it.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they crackle, add raw peanuts, chana dal, and urad dal.
Fry on low heat until peanuts turn crunchy and lentils turn golden brown.
Add slit green chillies, grated ginger, and fresh curry leaves; fry for 30 seconds, then turn off the flame completely.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice into the hot oil with salt, then pour this aromatic tadka over the rice and mix gently with a flat spatula.

name: Tomato Rice (Thakkali Sadam)
description: Tangy and spiced South Indian rice cooked with ripe country tomatoes, onions, and aromatic garam masala.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Temper mustard seeds, fennel seeds, a small cinnamon stick, and curry leaves.
Add sliced onions and ginger-garlic paste; sauté until onions turn translucent and sweet.
Add 3 finely chopped ripe country tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and coriander powder.
Cook covered on medium flame until tomatoes turn completely soft, pulpy, and oil starts separating from the masala.
Add cooked rice and a spoon of ghee; mix gently until the rice is thoroughly coated in the spiced tomato gravy.

name: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
description: Soothing, cooling tempered yogurt rice garnished with roasted mustard, ginger, green chillies, and pomegranate pearls.
steps: While cooked rice is still warm, mash it lightly with the back of a cup or ladle so it turns soft.
Add 0.5 cup warm milk first (this keeps the curd rice from turning sour over time) and mix well, then fold in 1 cup fresh thick curd and salt.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a small pan. Crackle mustard seeds, urad dal, finely chopped ginger, green chillies, and curry leaves.
Pour the hot ghee tempering directly into the creamy curd rice and stir gently.
Garnish with ruby pomegranate pearls, fresh coriander, and roasted cashews. Chill before serving.

name: Tamarind Rice (Puliyodharai)
description: Iconic temple-style tangy tamarind rice spiced with roasted sesame, fenugreek powder, and crunchy peanuts.
steps: Soak a lemon-sized ball of tamarind in warm water and extract 1 cup of thick pulp.
Dry roast fenugreek seeds, dry red chillies, and coriander seeds; grind into a fragrant spice powder.
Heat 3 tbsp sesame oil (gingelly oil). Crackle mustard seeds, peanuts, chana dal, dry red chillies, and curry leaves.
Pour in the thick tamarind extract, turmeric, jaggery, salt, and half the ground spice powder. Simmer on low heat until it thickens into an oily shiny paste (pulikachal).
Mix the prepared pulikachal into warm cooked rice with the remaining spice powder and 1 tbsp raw sesame oil for authentic temple flavor.

name: Coconut Rice (Thengai Sadam)
description: Delicate, aromatic rice tossed with freshly grated coconut, cashews, mustard seeds, and pure coconut oil.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp pure coconut oil or ghee in a pan.
Add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, whole cashews, dry red chillies, and curry leaves; fry until cashews turn golden.
Add finely slit green chillies, grated ginger, and a pinch of asafoetida (hing).
Add 1 cup of freshly grated coconut and sauté gently on low flame for just 2 minutes (do not brown the coconut).
Turn off the flame, add cooled cooked rice and salt, and toss gently until the coconut aroma coats every grain.

name: Jeera Rice
description: Fragrant long-grain basmati rice tempered in pure desi ghee with crackling roasted cumin seeds and fresh coriander.
steps: Rinse basmati rice until water runs clear; soak for 20 minutes, then cook with whole spices until grains are long and 95% done.
Heat 2 tbsp pure cow ghee in a wide heavy pan on medium flame.
Add 1.5 tbsp whole cumin seeds (jeera), 1 bay leaf, 2 green cardamoms, and 1 slit green chilli; let cumin crackle and release nutty aroma.
Gently fold in the cooked fluffy basmati rice and season with salt.
Toss on low flame for 1 minute, garnish with finely chopped fresh coriander, and serve with dal tadka.

name: Ghee Rice (Neychoru)
description: Rich Malabar celebration rice cooked in pure ghee with caramelized golden onions, roasted cashews, and sultanas.
steps: Heat 3 tbsp pure desi ghee in a heavy pot. Fry whole cashews and raisins until cashews are golden and raisins puff up; remove.
In the same ghee, thinly slice 1 onion and fry until deep caramelized golden brown (birista); remove half for garnish.
Add whole spices: cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaf; sauté washed and drained kaima or basmati rice for 2 minutes in the ghee.
Pour 2 cups boiling water per cup of rice, add salt, cover tightly with lid, and cook on low flame for 10-12 minutes until water is absorbed.
Gently fluff the rice, top with fried onions, cashews, raisins, and an extra drizzle of melted cow ghee.

name: Mint Rice (Pudina Rice)
description: Refreshing, vibrant green rice flavored with fresh garden mint leaves, coriander, green chillies, and whole spices.
steps: In a blender, grind 1 packed cup fresh mint leaves, 0.5 cup coriander, 3 green chillies, 1 inch ginger, and 4 garlic cloves with 2 tbsp water into a vibrant green paste.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee or oil in a pan. Add bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon, and sliced onions; sauté until translucent.
Add the freshly ground pudina paste and sauté on medium heat for 3 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add cooked rice and salt; mix gently on low flame until the mint paste coats every single rice grain evenly.
Serve hot with cooling onion raita and roasted papad.

name: Coriander Rice (Kothimeera Annam)
description: Fragrant green rice prepared with a fresh ground paste of aromatic cilantro, green chillies, ginger, and cumin.
steps: Blend a large bunch of fresh coriander leaves with green chillies, garlic, ginger, and cumin seeds into a smooth paste.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds, chana dal, urad dal, and crunchy peanuts; fry until golden.
Pour in the fresh coriander paste and sauté on low heat for 2-3 minutes until the vibrant green aroma blooms.
Stir in warm cooked rice and salt, toss gently on low heat, and serve with potato fry or curd.

name: Mango Rice (Mamidikaya Annam)
description: Seasonal Andhra specialty made with freshly grated raw tangy green mango, green chillies, and crunchy tempering.
steps: Peel and coarsely grate 1 firm, tart raw green mango.
Heat 2 tbsp groundnut oil in a kadai. Crackle mustard seeds, peanuts, chana dal, urad dal, slit green chillies, and curry leaves.
Add 0.5 tsp turmeric and the freshly grated raw mango; sauté on medium-low flame for 2-3 minutes until soft.
Turn off the heat, add cooked rice and salt, and mix thoroughly so the sour, tangy mango flavor permeates the rice.
Let sit for 10 minutes before serving to let the flavors deepen.

name: Sambar Rice (Sambar Sadam)
description: Wholesome, comforting one-pot rice simmered with spiced toor dal, mixed country vegetables, and aromatic ghee.
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with a pinch of turmeric and extra water until soft and mashable.
In a large pot, cook drumsticks, carrots, shallots, and beans with tamarind water, sambar powder, and salt until vegetables are tender.
Add cooked dal, cooked rice, and 1 cup of warm water; mash lightly so the rice and dal merge into a porridge-like consistency.
Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes so the rice absorbs the spicy tamarind sambar.
In a small pan, prepare a rich tadka of mustard, curry leaves, hing, and ghee; pour sizzling over the sambar rice and mix.

name: Rasam Rice
description: Warm, soul-soothing comforting rice soaked in hot, peppery tomato-garlic rasam, topped with pure ghee.
steps: Crush black peppercorns, cumin seeds, garlic, and dry red chilli coarsely.
Boil crushed tomatoes with tamarind water, turmeric, crushed spice paste, curry leaves, and salt for 7-8 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, hing, and curry leaves in hot ghee, pour into the boiling rasam, and turn off heat.
In a wide serving bowl, place warm cooked rice and pour 2 generous ladles of boiling peppery rasam over it.
Top with a teaspoon of pure cow ghee, mash gently with fingers or spoon, and enjoy hot.

name: Dal Rice (Pappu Annam)
description: Simple everyday comfort: hot rice mixed with homestyle seasoned yellow lentils, a generous spoon of cow ghee, and pickle.
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with water and a pinch of turmeric until creamy and fully cooked.
Mash the dal smooth with salt. Temper mustard seeds, cumin, crushed garlic, and curry leaves in pure cow ghee.
On a traditional plate or thali, serve steaming hot rice, ladle hot mashed dal directly over the center.
Top with a generous spoonful of melting pure desi cow ghee.
Mix with fingers and enjoy alongside Andhra avakaya pickle and crispy papad.

name: Chicken Rice
description: Hearty, comforting homestyle rice cooked with tender spiced chicken pieces, caramelized onions, and whole spices.
steps: Cut 250g boneless chicken into small bite-sized pieces. Marinate with 0.5 tsp turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy kadai. Crackle cumin seeds and whole cinnamon-cloves.
Sauté finely sliced onions and slit green chillies on medium flame until deep golden brown.
Add marinated chicken pieces and sauté on medium-high heat for 5 minutes until chicken turns white and releases natural juices.
Add chopped ripe tomatoes and fresh curry leaves; cook covered for 5 minutes until chicken is tender and masala is thick and glossy.
Gently fold in warm cooked basmati rice, drizzle 1 tsp pure cow ghee, and toss on low flame for 2 minutes until every grain absorbs the chicken flavor. Garnish with chopped fresh coriander.

name: Egg Rice
description: Quick, protein-rich everyday rice stir-fried with seasoned scrambled eggs, sliced onions, and crushed black pepper.
steps: In a bowl, crack 3 fresh farm eggs, add a pinch of salt, crushed black pepper, and 1 tbsp water; whisk lightly for extra fluffiness.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan or kadai. Sauté finely chopped onions, slit green chillies, and fresh curry leaves until onions turn light golden.
Pour the whisked eggs into the pan; let sit undisturbed for 20 seconds, then gently scramble into soft, large curds on medium flame.
When eggs are 90% set, tip in cold, separated cooked rice.
Add 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, freshly cracked black pepper, and salt to taste.
Toss continuously on high flame for 2 minutes so the rice grains become aromatic, slightly toasted, and thoroughly coated with the scrambled egg. Serve hot with pickle.

name: Bagara Rice
description: Signature Hyderabadi aromatic wedding rice cooked with mint, whole shahi garam masala, and caramelized onions.
steps: Rinse and soak basmati rice for 20 minutes.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat 2 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil. Add shahi jeera, bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and star anise; sauté until fragrant.
Add thinly sliced onions and green chillies; sauté on medium flame until onions turn deep golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, fresh mint leaves, and coriander; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add soaked drained rice, fry for 1 minute, then pour 2 cups of boiling water with salt. Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 12 minutes.

name: Bisibele Bath
description: Authentic Karnataka royal spicy rice and lentil dish cooked with vegetables, tamarind, and freshly ground aromatic spices.
steps: Pressure cook rice and toor dal together with 4 cups of water until soft and mushy.
Cook diced carrots, beans, shallots, and peas with tamarind pulp, jaggery, salt, and 2 tbsp authentic bisibelebath powder.
Combine the mashed rice-dal with the cooked spiced vegetables and add warm water to achieve a semi-liquid consistency.
Simmer on low flame for 6-8 minutes so the rice absorbs all the rich spice and tamarind flavors.
Heat 3 tbsp ghee; fry whole cashews, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing until golden; pour over the boiling bisibele bath.

name: Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani
description: The king of biryanis: marinated chicken slow-cooked on dum with saffron-infused long grain basmati rice, mint, and fried onions.
steps: Marinate 500g chicken with thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, biryani masala, mint, coriander, and half the golden fried onions (birista) for at least 1 hour.
In a large pot of boiling water with whole garam masala and salt, boil soaked basmati rice until 70% done (firm to bite); drain.
Spread the marinated raw chicken evenly at the bottom of a heavy-bottomed handi.
Layer the 70% cooked hot basmati rice over the chicken. Drizzle saffron-infused warm milk, 3 tbsp pure desi ghee, rose water, and remaining fried onions on top.
Seal the rim of the pot tightly with dough or aluminum foil and lid. Cook on high heat for 10 minutes, then place on a heavy tawa on low heat for 25 minutes for dum cooking.
Rest for 10 minutes before gently scooping from the bottom to reveal layers of aromatic saffron rice and succulent chicken.

name: Chicken Fry Piece Biryani
description: Iconic Andhra style: fragrant spiced bagara rice topped with spicy, deep-roasted chicken fry and curry leaves.
steps: Prepare fragrant bagara rice: sauté shahi jeera, whole spices, mint, and onions in ghee; cook basmati rice until fluffy and set aside.
For chicken fry: marinate chicken pieces with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, coriander powder, pepper, and garam masala for 30 minutes.
Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy iron kadai. Sauté sliced onions, slit green chillies, and lots of fresh curry leaves.
Add marinated chicken and roast on medium-high flame without adding water until moisture evaporates and chicken turns deep roasted dark golden.
To serve: ladle hot aromatic bagara rice onto a platter, generously heap the spicy roasted chicken fry pieces over the top, and garnish with fried cashews.

name: Chicken 65 Biryani
description: Spicy, crispy fried Chicken 65 tossed with curry leaves, layered over aromatic dum basmati rice.
steps: Marinate the Chicken 65 with thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, mint, and freshly ground biryani spices for 45 minutes.
Parboil premium long-grain basmati rice with whole spices in boiling salted water until 70% done; drain carefully.
Cook the marinated Chicken 65 in a heavy pot with pure cow ghee until tender and aromatic.
Layer the fragrant basmati rice over the masala, drizzle saffron milk, ghee, and golden fried onions.
Seal with airtight lid and cook on gentle dum heat for 15-20 minutes to infuse the aromas.

name: Donne Chicken Biryani
description: Legendary Bangalore Shivaji Military Hotel specialty made with short-grain seeraga samba rice and aromatic green herbal masala.
steps: Blend a large bunch of fresh mint leaves, coriander, green chillies, garlic, ginger, and cinnamon-cloves into a fine green herbal masala paste.
Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot. Add whole spices, sliced onions, and sauté until translucent.
Add chicken pieces and the freshly ground green herbal paste; sauté on medium flame for 5 minutes until oil starts releasing.
Add washed short-grain seeraga samba rice and gently coat the rice in the green masala for 2 minutes.
Pour boiling water (1:2 ratio), add salt, bring to a boil, cover tightly, and cook on low flame for 12 minutes until water is absorbed.
Serve piping hot in traditional eco-friendly palm leaf cups (donne) with onion raita and boiled egg.

name: Ambur Chicken Biryani
description: Famous Tamil Nadu Arcot specialty cooked with seeraga samba rice, red chilli paste, curd, and tender chicken.
steps: Soak seeraga samba rice for 20 minutes.
Soak dry red chillies in warm water and grind into a smooth red paste.
In a heavy brass pot, heat oil and ghee. Sauté thinly sliced onions until golden; add ginger-garlic paste and the fresh red chilli paste.
Add chopped tomatoes, curd, and chicken pieces; cook on medium heat until chicken releases its juices and gravy thickens.
Cook seeraga samba rice in boiling salted water until 70% done; drain and layer over the chicken masala.
Cover tightly with lid and place burning coals or heavy weight on top for 20 minutes dum. Serve with brinjal gravy (ennai kathirikai).

name: Dindigul Chicken Biryani
description: Signature Dindigul Thalappakatti biryani made with succulent country chicken, seeraga samba rice, and freshly pounded pepper masala.
steps: Pound whole black peppercorns, cumin, shallots (small sambar onions), ginger, and garlic into a coarse rustic paste.
Heat ghee in a pot. Sauté the shallot-pepper paste and fresh mint until aromatic.
Add tender chicken pieces, fresh thick curd, lemon juice, and salt; simmer on medium flame until chicken is half-cooked.
Add drained seeraga samba rice and boiling water. Stir once gently.
Cook until water level aligns with rice, then seal with lid and place on low dum for 15 minutes. The signature peppery aroma will fill the kitchen.

name: Malabar Chicken Biryani
description: Kerala Thalassery style biryani cooked with fragrant kaima rice, mild spices, fried cashews, raisins, and tender chicken.
steps: Marinate chicken with turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice, and salt; shallow fry lightly and set aside.
Sauté thinly sliced onions, tomatoes, ginger-garlic-green chilli paste, fennel powder, and garam masala to make a rich Malabar chicken gravy.
For rice: heat ghee, sauté whole spices, and fry kaima / jeerakasala rice for 2 minutes. Add boiling water and cook until fluffy.
In a heavy vessel, layer the chicken gravy, then cooked fragrant kaima rice, followed by fried cashews, raisins, fried onions, and a sprinkle of garam masala.
Seal and place on low dum for 15 minutes. Serve with date-lemon pickle and coconut chammanthi.

name: Chicken Tikka Biryani
description: Charcoal tandoor-smoked marinated chicken tikka chunks layered with aromatic saffron rice and brown onions.
steps: Marinate the Chicken Tikka with thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, mint, and freshly ground biryani spices for 45 minutes.
Parboil premium long-grain basmati rice with whole spices in boiling salted water until 70% done; drain carefully.
Cook the marinated Chicken Tikka in a heavy pot with pure cow ghee until tender and aromatic.

Seal with airtight lid and cook on gentle dum heat for 15-20 minutes to infuse the aromas.

name: Egg Dum Biryani
description: Boiled eggs shallow-fried with turmeric and chilli, layered with aromatic saffron basmati rice and mint.
steps: Hard-boil 4 eggs; make small shallow slits on the sides. Toss in a pan with 0.5 tsp turmeric, chilli powder, and 1 tsp ghee until outer skin turns blistered and golden.
Cook basmati rice with bay leaf, cloves, and salt until 75% done; drain.
In a pot, prepare a rich biryani gravy by sautéing onions, ginger-garlic, tomatoes, curd, biryani masala, and mint.
Gently nestle the golden fried eggs into the gravy.
Layer the drained basmati rice over the eggs, drizzle saffron milk, ghee, and golden fried onions. Cover tightly on low dum for 12 minutes.

description: Spicy pan-roasted eggs with crispy onions and curry leaves, topped over fragrant biryani rice.
steps: Marinate the Egg Fry with thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, mint, and freshly ground biryani spices for 45 minutes.

name: Prawn Biryani (Royyala Biryani)
description: Juicy, succulent ocean prawns marinated in coastal spices, layered with fragrant basmati rice and coriander.
steps: Clean and devein fresh prawns. Marinate with 1 tsp turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee. Sauté onions, green chillies, tomatoes, and biryani spices until soft and fragrant.
Add marinated prawns and cook for just 3-4 minutes on medium flame (do not overcook prawns or they become rubbery).
Layer partially cooked basmati rice over the juicy prawn masala.
Drizzle saffron milk, mint, and pure ghee; seal and dum cook for just 10 minutes on very low heat.

name: Fish Biryani
description: Delicate kingfish steaks marinated in ginger, garlic, and turmeric, gently layered with fragrant spiced rice.
steps: Marinate the Fish with thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, mint, and freshly ground biryani spices for 45 minutes.
Parboil premium long-grain basmati rice with whole spices in boiling salted water until 70% done; drain carefully.
Cook the marinated Fish in a heavy pot with pure cow ghee until tender and aromatic.

name: Vegetable Dum Biryani
description: Colorful medley of cauliflower, carrots, beans, and potatoes cooked with mint, fried onions, and saffron basmati rice.
steps: Cut carrots, French beans, cauliflower florets, and potatoes into even bite-sized pieces.
Marinate the vegetables in thick curd, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, red chilli powder, mint, coriander, and fried onions for 30 minutes.
Cook vegetables in a wide pot with 2 tbsp ghee for 5-6 minutes until half-cooked.
Parboil soaked basmati rice with whole spices in salted water until 70% done; drain.
Layer the aromatic rice over the vegetable masala, drizzle saffron milk and pure ghee, seal with foil, and dum cook on low heat for 20 minutes.

name: Paneer Biryani
description: Marinated succulent cubes of paneer layered with fragrant long-grain basmati rice, fried onions, and mint.
steps: Cut fresh paneer into 1-inch cubes. Marinate with curd, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, kasuri methi, and salt for 20 minutes.
Lightly pan-sear the paneer cubes in ghee for 2 minutes until aromatic (do not overcook).
Prepare a spiced onion-tomato gravy with mint and coriander in the pot, then fold in the marinated paneer.
Layer 75% cooked basmati rice over the paneer masala, sprinkle fried onions and ghee.
Cook on low dum for 12 minutes until the rice is fragrant and paneer remains pillow-soft.

name: Kaju Biryani (Cashew Biryani)
description: Rich, royal Andhra restaurant specialty loaded with golden roasted cashews, fried onions, and ghee basmati rice.
steps: Heat 3 tbsp pure cow ghee in a heavy pot. Fry 1 cup of whole cashews on low heat until rich golden and crunchy; set half aside for garnish.
In the remaining ghee, sauté shahi jeera, whole garam masala, and sliced onions until deep golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, green chillies, tomatoes, curd, and biryani masala; cook until oil releases.
Add the roasted cashews and fold in parboiled fragrant basmati rice.
Drizzle saffron milk, cover with airtight lid, and cook on low dum for 15 minutes. Garnish with remaining crisp cashews.

name: Veg Pulao
description: Fragrant, mild one-pot basmati rice cooked with mixed vegetables, whole spices, and a dash of ghee.
steps: Soak long-grain basmati rice for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a pressure cooker or heavy pot. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.
Add sliced onions, slit green chillies, ginger-garlic paste, and sauté until fragrant.
Add diced carrots, green peas, beans, and potatoes; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add drained basmati rice, gently mix with vegetables, pour 2 cups warm water per cup of rice, add salt, cover, and cook for 1 whistle on medium flame or 12 mins on low heat.

name: Peas Pulao (Matar Pulao)
description: Classic North Indian homestyle rice simmered with sweet green peas, cumin seeds, and whole cinnamon.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp pure cow ghee in a pot. Add 1 tbsp cumin seeds, 2 green cardamoms, and 1 black cardamom; sauté until cumin crackles.
Add thinly sliced onions and sauté until soft and translucent (do not brown).
Add 1 cup fresh or frozen sweet green peas and sauté for 1 minute.
Add soaked and drained basmati rice and gently fry in ghee for 1 minute.
Pour 2 cups of boiling water, add salt, cover with lid, and cook on low flame for 12 minutes until water is absorbed and grains are fluffy.

name: Mushroom Pulao
description: Mild, aromatic rice tossed with sliced button mushrooms, garlic, and ground spices.
steps: Heat pure cow ghee in a heavy pot. Crackle cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.
Sauté onions and ingredients for Mushroom Pulao until aromatic and sweet.
Add soaked basmati rice, pour warm water or seasoned stock, and season with salt.
Cover tightly and simmer on low heat until grains are long, fluffy, and fragrant.

name: Kaju Pulao
description: Delicately spiced festive rice generously studded with golden pan-roasted whole cashew nuts.
steps: Heat pure cow ghee in a heavy pot. Crackle cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.

name: Kashmiri Pulao
description: Exotic, mildly sweet royal rice infused with saffron, garnished with pomegranate, apple, walnuts, and fried onions.
steps: Infuse a generous pinch of Kashmiri saffron strands in 3 tbsp warm milk.
Heat 3 tbsp ghee; fry whole almonds, cashews, and walnuts until golden; remove and set aside.
In the same ghee, sauté whole spices (cinnamon, cloves, fennel seeds) and basmati rice.
Pour water, saffron milk, and salt; cook covered until rice is fragrant, fluffy, and golden yellow.
Gently fluff the rice, fold in the roasted dry fruits, and garnish with fresh pomegranate seeds and thin apple slices.

name: Tawa Pulao
description: Mumbai street food specialty: fluffy rice tossed on a huge iron tawa with pav bhaji masala, butter, and crunchy capsicum.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp butter on a wide tawa or flat pan. Sauté cumin seeds, finely chopped onions, and ginger-garlic paste.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
Add diced capsicum, boiled green peas, 1.5 tbsp pav bhaji masala, red chilli powder, and salt; cook for 2 minutes.
Tip in cold leftover cooked rice and 1 extra tbsp butter.
Toss vigorously on high flame with a spatula until the rice turns rich spicy orange-red. Squeeze fresh lemon juice on top.

steps: Heat pure cow ghee in a heavy pot. Crackle cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.

name: Dal Khichdi
description: Comfort in a bowl: wholesome yellow moong lentils and rice simmered to creamy perfection, topped with garlic ghee tadka.
steps: Wash 0.5 cup rice and 0.5 cup yellow moong dal together; pressure cook with 3.5 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 4 whistles until creamy.
For the royal tadka: heat 2 tbsp pure cow ghee in a small pan.
Add 1 tbsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 6 cloves of finely chopped garlic, 2 slit green chillies, and curry leaves.
Fry on medium flame until garlic turns golden brown and deeply fragrant.
Pour the sizzling garlic ghee tadka directly over the creamy hot khichdi, stir gently, and serve with papad and pickle.

steps: Heat pure cow ghee in a heavy pot. Crackle cumin seeds, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves.

name: Ghee Karam Rice
description: Homestyle Andhra comfort: steaming hot rice mixed with pure cow ghee and authentic spicy garlic karam podi.
steps: Take piping hot, freshly cooked steamed rice in a traditional bowl.
Make a small depression in the center and add 2-3 tablespoons of authentic Andhra spicy garlic karam podi (gunpowder).
Heat 3 tablespoons of pure desi cow ghee until smoking hot, and pour directly over the podi.
Watch the ghee sizzle and release the intoxicating roasted aroma of garlic and spices.
Mix with your fingers while hot and savor the comforting homestyle Andhra flavors.

name: Pani Puri (Golgappa / Puchka)
description: Crisp hollow puris stuffed with spiced potato-chickpea mash, dipped in chilled spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
steps: For spicy pani (teekha pani): Blend fresh mint leaves, coriander, green chillies, ginger, and lemon juice into a fine paste. Mix with 3 cups chilled water, black salt, roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and boondi.
For sweet pani (meetha pani): Dilute thick tamarind-date chutney with 1.5 cups chilled water and a pinch of roasted cumin powder.
For filling: Coarsely mash boiled potatoes with boiled brown chickpeas, red chilli powder, chaat masala, and chopped coriander.
To assemble: Poke a hole in the center of a crisp hollow puri with your thumb.
Stuff with a spoonful of the potato-chickpea mixture, add a dash of sweet tamarind chutney, dunk completely into the spicy mint water, and pop the whole puri into your mouth immediately!

name: Bhel Puri
description: Iconic Mumbai beach snack: crunchy puffed rice, sev, and crushed papdi tossed with onions, boiled potatoes, and tangy chutneys.
steps: Ensure the puffed rice (murmura) is completely dry and crunchy (dry roast in a pan for 2 minutes if soft).
In a large mixing bowl, combine puffed rice, crushed flat papdis, finely diced boiled potatoes, chopped onions, and deseeded tomatoes.
Add 2 tablespoons of spicy green mint-coriander chutney and 2 tablespoons of sweet-tangy tamarind chutney.
Sprinkle chaat masala, black salt, and squeeze fresh lemon juice over the mixture.
Toss quickly and vigorously with two spoons so the chutneys coat the murmura without making it soggy.
Top generously with a mountain of fine nylon sev and fresh coriander; serve immediately in paper cones.

name: Sev Puri
description: Flat crispy papdis topped with spiced potato-onion mash, trio of chutneys, raw mango pieces, and an avalanche of fine sev.
steps: Arrange 6 to 8 crisp flat papdis in a single layer on a serving plate.
Top each papdi with a spoonful of diced boiled potatoes and finely chopped onions.
Drizzle fiery red garlic chutney, vibrant spicy green mint chutney, and glossy sweet tamarind chutney over every papdi.
Add a sprinkle of finely chopped raw green mango (kacchi kairi) for a signature Mumbai tang.
Dust generously with chaat masala and roasted cumin powder.
Completely bury the puris under a mountain of golden nylon sev and chopped cilantro; eat immediately while crispy.

name: Dahi Puri
description: Crispy puris stuffed with spiced potatoes, drenched in chilled sweetened whisked curd, tamarind glaze, and crunchy sev.
steps: Whisk 1.5 cups fresh thick curd with 1.5 tbsp powdered sugar and a pinch of black salt until silky smooth and chilled.
Place 6 to 8 hollow puris on a plate and crack a hole in the center of each.
Stuff each puri with a spoonful of seasoned potato mash and boiled moong or chickpeas.
Drizzle sweet tamarind-date chutney and spicy green chutney inside each puri.
Generously ladle the cold sweetened curd over each puri until they are completely bathed in white yogurt.
Garnish with a drizzle of tamarind chutney, a dusting of red chilli powder and chaat masala, fine sev, and ruby pomegranate pearls.

name: Masala Puri
description: Bangalore street food legend: crushed crispy puris smothered in piping hot spiced dried green peas gravy with onions and sev.
steps: Pressure cook soaked dried green peas with turmeric and salt until soft; mash half the peas for a thick curry consistency.
Prepare the spiced gravy: Sauté onions, ginger, garlic, tomatoes, and ground spices (cinnamon, cloves, fennel, coriander) into a spicy sauce; simmer with the mashed green peas for 5 minutes.
In a shallow bowl, coarsely crush 4 to 5 crisp puris with your fingers.
Ladle 2 generous ladles of the boiling hot green peas gravy all over the crushed puris.
Top immediately with finely chopped onions, grated carrots, fresh coriander, sweet tamarind chutney, and fine sev.
Enjoy piping hot with a spoon while the puris are semi-crisp and soaking in the spiced gravy.

name: Samosa
description: Pyramid-shaped flaky pastry crust stuffed with a spiced potato-green peas filling, deep-fried to golden perfection.
steps: For the flaky crust: Rub 3 tbsp hot ghee or oil into 2 cups maida with ajwain and salt until it forms breadcrumb texture (moin). Knead into a very stiff, firm dough; rest 20 minutes.
For stuffing: Sauté cumin, crushed coriander seeds, ginger, and green chillies in oil. Add boiled potatoes crushed by hand, green peas, amchur, garam masala, and cashews; cook 3 minutes until dry.
Roll oval-shaped discs of dough, slice in half into semi-circles.
Apply water along the straight edge, fold into a cone shape, seal the seam firmly, and stuff generously with the spiced potato filling.
Pleat the back edge, seal the base tightly so the samosa can stand upright on a flat surface.

Slide into medium-low heat oil (do not fry in smoking oil or bubbles will form). Fry slowly on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until pale golden, then increase heat for 2 minutes to a deep, blister-free golden crunch.

name: Onion Samosa (Irani / Street Samosa)
description: Thin, ultra-crispy translucent pastry pockets packed with a spicy raw onion, poha, and green chilli filling.
steps: Thinly slice 3 large onions. Mix with 0.5 cup raw thin poha (poha absorbs excess moisture from the onions during frying to ensure maximum crispiness).
Add finely chopped green chillies, red chilli powder, garam masala, salt, and lots of fresh chopped coriander; mix well.
Use thin samosa patti strips. Fold one corner to form a triangle pocket.
Fill with the spiced raw onion-poha mixture (do not overfill).
Apply a flour-water paste on the edges and fold securely to seal all three corners completely.
Drop into medium-hot oil and deep-fry on medium flame for 4 to 5 minutes until wafer-thin, golden, and crackling crisp. Serve with hot chai.

name: Mirchi Bajji (Mirapakaya Bajji)
description: Andhra street classic: thick green bhavnagri chillies stuffed with ajwain-tamarind masala, dipped in gram flour batter, and double-fried.
steps: Wash and slit large thick bajji chillies lengthwise; deseed with the back of a spoon to reduce heat.
For stuffing: Mix 1 tbsp carom seeds (ajwain), 1 tbsp roasted cumin powder, salt, and thick tamarind pulp into a paste. Stuff inside each slit chilli.
Whisk 1 cup besan, 2 tbsp rice flour (for crunch), salt, turmeric, a pinch of baking soda, and water into a smooth, lump-free, thick batter.
Hold each stuffed chilli by its stem, dip completely into the batter to coat evenly, and slide into hot oil.
Deep-fry on medium flame for 4 minutes until golden; drain.
For street style: Slit the fried bajji open, stuff with finely chopped raw onions tossed in lemon juice and chaat masala, and serve piping hot.

name: Aloo Bajji (Potato Fritters)
description: Thin round slices of potato enveloped in a spiced gram flour batter, deep-fried into puffed golden pillows.
steps: Peel 2 large potatoes and slice into even, thin rounds (about 2 mm thick) using a mandoline slicer. Soak in cold salted water for 5 minutes, then pat completely dry.
Prepare batter: In a bowl, whisk 1 cup besan, 2 tbsp rice flour, ajwain, chilli powder, hing, salt, and water into a thick, pourable batter.
Add 1 tablespoon of smoking hot oil and a tiny pinch of baking soda into the batter; whisk briskly for 1 minute for extra puffiness.
Dip each potato slice into the batter, coating both sides thoroughly.
Slide gently into medium-hot oil. The slices will puff up like pillows within seconds.
Fry on both sides for 3 minutes until crisp and golden brown; serve hot with green chutney.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: Mumbai's most beloved street food: rich mashed spiced vegetable gravy swimming in butter, served with soft griddle-toasted pav.
steps: Pressure cook potatoes, cauliflower, carrots, and green peas with water and salt until completely soft; mash smooth with a potato masher.
Heat 2 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp oil in a wide pan or flat tawa. Sauté finely chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste until golden.
Add finely diced capsicum and sauté for 2 minutes; add chopped ripe tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy.
Add 2.5 tbsp authentic pav bhaji masala, 1 tbsp bright red Kashmiri chilli powder, and salt. Cook until butter starts separating.
Add the mashed boiled vegetables and 1 cup of warm water. Mash continuously with the masher on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until thick and glossy.
Finish with a giant block of butter, fresh lemon juice, and coriander.
Slice pav buns horizontally. Toast on a hot tawa with a generous dollop of butter, a pinch of pav bhaji masala, and coriander until golden and soft.
Serve steaming bhaji topped with extra melting butter, alongside the warm buttered pav, sliced onions, and lemon wedges.

name: Vada Pav
description: The Mumbai burger: spiced batata vada inside a soft pav lined with dry red garlic-peanut chutney and green chutney.
steps: For potato filling: Heat 1 tbsp oil; crackle mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves, and pounded ginger-garlic-green chilli paste. Add turmeric, salt, and coarsely mashed boiled potatoes. Sauté 2 minutes, finish with coriander, and shape into round balls.
For batter: Whisk besan, rice flour, turmeric, salt, a pinch of baking soda, and water into a smooth dipping batter.
Dip each potato ball into the batter, coating completely, and drop into hot oil.
Deep-fry on medium flame for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp; drain.
Slit a soft ladi pav horizontally (leaving the hinge intact).
Spread spicy green mint chutney on the bottom and a generous layer of authentic fiery dry red garlic-peanut chutney inside.
Place the hot batata vada inside, press gently, and serve with a salted fried green chilli.

name: Dabeli (Kutchi Dabeli)
description: Gujarat street food favorite: sweet and spicy potato mash stuffed in pav with masala peanuts, pomegranate, and sev.
steps: In a pan, heat 1 tbsp oil. Sauté 2 tbsp dabeli masala with 3 tbsp sweet-tangy tamarind chutney until fragrant.
Add mashed boiled potatoes and 2-3 tbsp water; mix into a smooth, moist, spiced potato spread. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Spread the potato mixture onto a flat plate. Decorate the top with fresh pomegranate pearls, spicy masala peanuts, chopped coriander, and fine sev.
Slit pav buns, apply sweet tamarind chutney and spicy garlic chutney inside.
Stuff generously with the prepared potato mixture, extra masala peanuts, and pomegranate.
Toast the stuffed dabeli on a hot tawa with generous butter on all sides until golden.
Roll the exposed edges in a bowl of nylon sev so it sticks all around, and serve warm.

name: Aloo Tikki
description: Delhi-style pan-crisped potato patties with a golden crackling crust, topped with spiced curd and chutneys.
steps: Boil potatoes, let them cool completely in the fridge (chilling removes moisture for a crisper crust), then grate finely.
Mix grated potatoes with 2 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tbsp rice flour, minced green chillies, grated ginger, chaat masala, and salt into a smooth dough.
Shape into thick, round 2.5-inch patties with smooth edges.
Heat 3 tbsp ghee or oil on a flat heavy tawa on medium flame.
Place patties on the tawa and shallow-fry slowly for 5-6 minutes on each side, pressing gently with a flat spatula until the exterior forms a deep golden, crackling, ultra-crisp crust.
Serve hot as standalone tikkis or crush on a plate topped with whisked sweet curd, tamarind chutney, mint chutney, and sev.

name: Chole Bhature
description: Punjabi royal breakfast: balloon-puffed giant fermented bhature served with dark, intensely spiced Amritsari chole.
steps: For chole: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with a black tea bag (for deep authentic dark color), cinnamon, and black cardamom until melt-in-mouth soft.

Sauté onions, ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, chole masala, amchur, and coriander powder in ghee until oil separates. Simmer cooked chole with the gravy for 10 minutes, lightly mashing some chickpeas to thicken.

For bhature dough: Knead 2 cups maida with 2 tbsp sooji, 0.5 cup curd, 0.5 tsp baking powder, pinch of baking soda, sugar, and warm water into a soft, elastic dough. Rest covered with a damp cloth for 2 hours.
Divide into smooth balls, roll into large 7-inch oval sheets with light oil (do not use dry flour).
Slide into smoking hot oil in a deep kadai. Immediately tap the bhatura lightly with a slotted ladle; it will puff into a giant golden balloon!
Flip for 5 seconds until pale golden, drain, and serve immediately alongside hot Amritsari chole, pickled green chillies, and sliced red onions.

name: Veg Hakka Noodles
description: Desi Indo-Chinese street style boiled noodles tossed on high flame with julienned vegetables, soy sauce, and black pepper.
steps: Boil noodles in salted water until 80% al dente; drain immediately, rinse in cold water, and toss with 1 tsp oil to keep strands separate.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a smoking hot wok on the highest flame.
Add finely minced garlic and sliced onions; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add julienned carrots, capsicum, and shredded cabbage; toss vigorously on high flame for 1.5 minutes to retain crunch.
Add the boiled noodles, 1.5 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp green chilli sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, and freshly cracked black pepper.
Using two tongs, toss noodles continuously on high flame for 2 minutes until smoky and well coated. Garnish with spring onions.

name: Egg Noodles
description: Street-style wok-tossed noodles with scrambled eggs, shredded cabbage, carrots, and piquant Chinese sauces.
steps: Boil noodles until al dente, drain, rinse with cold water, and coat with 1 tsp oil.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a hot wok; pour 2 whisked eggs seasoned with pepper and quickly scramble into soft ribbons; remove.
In the same wok, heat 1 tbsp oil on high flame, sauté minced garlic and spring onions.
Add shredded vegetables and toss for 1 minute.
Add noodles, scrambled eggs, soy sauce, chilli sauce, and black pepper; toss on high flame for 2 minutes until hot and fragrant.

name: Chicken Noodles
description: Tender seasoned chicken strips stir-fried with noodles, vegetables, garlic, and savory umami sauces.
steps: Marinate thin strips of chicken breast with 0.5 tsp soy sauce, cornstarch, pepper, and salt for 10 minutes.
Stir-fry chicken strips in 2 tbsp oil on high flame for 3-4 minutes until cooked through and golden; push to the side.
Quickly scramble 1 egg in the center of the wok.
Add minced garlic, julienned cabbage, carrots, and capsicum; toss on smoking high flame.
Add boiled noodles, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauce, and cracked black pepper; toss vigorously for 2 minutes.

name: Schezwan Noodles
description: Fiery and spicy red noodles tossed with homemade Schezwan sauce, garlic, and crunchy vegetables.
steps: Boil noodles until al dente, rinse in cold water, and toss with oil.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high heat; sauté minced garlic, ginger, and spring onions.
Add julienned vegetables and stir-fry for 1.5 minutes.
Add 2 generous tablespoons of spicy red Schezwan sauce and 1 tsp soy sauce; stir until bubbling.
Toss in the noodles and stir-fry on high flame until every strand is coated in fiery red sauce. Garnish with scallions.

name: Chicken Schezwan Noodles
description: Spicy street food favorite: tender chicken strips tossed with noodles in fiery Schezwan sauce and crunchy vegetables.
steps: Sear sliced chicken breast in 2 tbsp oil until golden and cooked.
Add minced garlic, sliced carrots, and cabbage; toss on high heat for 1 minute.
Stir in 2.5 tablespoons of Schezwan sauce and soy sauce.
Add boiled noodles and toss vigorously on high flame so the spicy red sauce glazes the chicken and noodles evenly.

name: Veg Steamed Momos
description: Delicate, translucent steamed dumplings stuffed with finely minced cabbage, carrots, onions, garlic, and black pepper.
steps: Knead 1.5 cups maida with water and a pinch of salt into a smooth, firm dough; rest covered for 20 minutes.
For filling: Mix finely grated cabbage, carrots, onions, minced garlic, ginger, black pepper, 1 tsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oil, and salt. Squeeze lightly to remove excess water.
Divide dough into small marble-sized balls; roll into very thin 3-inch discs with thinner edges and slightly thicker center.
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the center.
Pleat the edges from one side to the other, pinching tightly to create the classic crescent or round pouch shape.
Grease steamer plates with oil, arrange momos leaving space between them, and steam on high heat for 8 to 10 minutes until skins turn translucent and glossy. Serve with spicy red chilli-garlic dip.

name: Chicken Steamed Momos
description: Juicy, succulent steamed dumplings stuffed with seasoned minced chicken, scallions, and ginger-garlic.
steps: In a bowl, mix minced chicken with finely chopped onions, spring onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, black pepper, and 1 tbsp melted butter (butter keeps chicken momos juicy inside).
Roll thin circular wrappers from rested dough.
Place filling in the center, pleat and pinch the edges together to seal tightly.
Steam on high heat for 10 to 12 minutes until wrappers are shiny and chicken is fully cooked.
Serve piping hot with fiery red momo chutney.

name: Fried Chicken Momos
description: Crispy golden deep-fried dumplings with a crackling outer shell and juicy chicken filling.
steps: Prepare chicken momos and steam lightly for 5 minutes (half-steam prevents dough from getting chewy during frying).
Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium flame.
Drop the prepared momos into medium-hot oil.
Deep-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning gently until the outer wrapper turns uniformly golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and dust with a pinch of peri-peri or chaat masala; serve hot with mayonnaise and red chilli sauce.

name: Tandoori Momos
description: Delhi street innovation: steamed momos coated in a spicy hung curd tandoori marinade, roasted to smoky perfection.
steps: Whisk thick curd with mustard oil, Kashmiri chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and lemon juice into a rich red tandoori marinade.
Gently coat steamed momos with the marinade; let sit for 10 minutes.
Skewer or place on a greased grill pan / tawa.
Roast on high heat with butter or over direct flame for 4-5 minutes until blistered with smoky charred spots.
Toss with chaat masala, lemon juice, and sliced onions; serve hot with mint chutney.

name: Kurkure Momos
description: Ultra-crunchy fried momos coated in a seasoned cornflake crumb crust, served with spicy dip.
steps: Crush plain cornflakes coarsely with hands or rolling pin.
Make a smooth medium-thick slurry with maida, cornstarch, chilli flakes, and water.
Dip each steamed momo into the slurry, then roll thoroughly in the crushed cornflakes to coat all sides evenly.
Heat oil on medium flame.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the cornflake crust turns deep golden and super crunchy. Serve hot.

name: Chicken Kathi Roll
description: Kolkata style street wrap: flaky paratha layered with fried egg, stuffed with spiced chicken tikka, sliced onions, and green chutney.
steps: Sauté marinated chicken tikka pieces in 1 tbsp oil until juicy and charred around edges.
Cook a flaky layered paratha on a tawa with ghee.
Crack an egg on the tawa, season with salt and pepper, and place the paratha directly on top of the raw egg; press so they stick together into an egg-paratha.
Flip and cook for 30 seconds until egg is set; place on greaseproof paper egg-side up.
Arrange the spiced chicken cubes along the center, top with thinly sliced red onions, a drizzle of spicy green chutney, sweet tomato sauce, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
Roll tightly into a parchment paper cylinder and serve hot.

name: Egg Roll
description: Crispy golden paratha fried with double eggs, rolled with crunchy raw onions, green chillies, and tangy chaat masala.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil on a flat tawa; pour 2 whisked eggs.
Place a paratha or flatbread directly over the wet egg, press firmly, and cook until the egg bonds with the paratha.
Flip and toast until the paratha is crisp and golden; transfer to paper.
Layer thinly sliced onions, chopped green chillies, chaat masala, lemon juice, and a drizzle of tomato sauce along the center.
Roll up tightly and serve hot.

name: Paneer Kathi Roll
description: Flaky whole wheat paratha wrapped around spiced paneer tikka, crunchy bell peppers, sliced onions, and mint chutney.
steps: Marinate paneer cubes and sliced bell peppers in curd, tandoori masala, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice for 15 minutes.
Sauté on high heat in a pan with butter for 3-4 minutes until paneer is lightly charred.
Warm a flaky paratha on the tawa.
